sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Buncombe County?
sections.html:
Buncombe County runs property tax through its Tax Assessment office at 182 College Street in Asheville, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 5 pm. The assessor lists, appraises and assesses all taxable property, and the collector bills and collects the tax.

Different desks answer different questions, so call the one that fits.

  • Real estate assessment and appeals: 828-250-4940
  • Property tax collections and payment plans: 828-250-4910
  • Exemptions and senior or disability relief: 828-250-4915
  • Business and personal property listings: 828-250-4930
  • Land records: 828-250-4970

Bills, property record cards and appeal requests are available by searching an address at tax.buncombenc.gov. If you are selling a house in Buncombe County, the collections desk can tell you what is owed on the parcel before closing.

sections.h2: Why are 2026 Buncombe County tax bills based on 2021 values?
sections.html:
A new state law delayed the county's 2026 reappraisal until January 1, 2027, so 2026 bills use the values set in the 2021 reappraisal. Buncombe County had done its reappraisal with values effective January 1, 2026, and mailed new values to owners earlier in the year.

In July 2026 the legislature passed two measures, S.B. 889 (S.L. 2026-8) and S.B. 474 (S.L. 2026-47). The first pushed use of the 2026 schedule of values back a year in a limited group of counties that includes Buncombe. The second let the county keep the 2026 values only if it adopted a revenue-neutral rate, which the county said would round to 40 cents per $100. At a special meeting on July 14, 2026, the commissioners chose the older values with a higher rate, citing the budget adopted on June 2, 2026.

For most owners the practical result is simple. Unless you added or changed improvements, your 2026 value matches last year's, and last year's value already reflected any Tropical Storm Helene adjustment. Bills were delayed and went online before the mail run.

sections.h2: What are the Buncombe County property tax rates?
sections.html:
The county rate adopted for the 2026 bills is 61.54 cents per $100 of assessed value, applied to the 2021 schedule. Your total rate also depends on special districts, so find the ones that cover your parcel on the tax site.

Buncombe County rates adopted at the July 14, 2026 special meeting
JurisdictionRate per $100 of assessed valueSource
Buncombe County61.54 centsCounty news release, July 14, 2026
Unified Fire District17.38 centsCounty news release, July 14, 2026
Asheville City Schools district11.75 centsCounty news release, July 14, 2026

The county sets values for every city, town and district inside its borders, so the delay also reached municipalities. The revenue-neutral option applied only to the county's own rate, not to the city or special districts. Asheville city and other municipal rates are set separately, so confirm them on your tax bill.

sections.h2: When is Buncombe County property tax due?
sections.html:
Bills are typically due September 1, and the county allows payment without penalty through January 5 of the following year. For the 2026 bills that grace period ran to January 5, 2027.

State law sets the interest that starts on January 6. The first stretch, January 6 to February 1, carries 2%, and after that interest builds at three quarters of one percent a month or fraction of a month. Mailed payments count as received on the postmark date.

Owners who cannot pay in one sum can ask Tax Collections about a payment plan. The county lists two types, a Casual Payment Plan and a Preauthorized Debit Payment Plan. Enrolled owners are not subject to collection actions such as wage or bank garnishment while they stay on the plan. Call 828-250-4910 to speak with a collection specialist.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Buncombe County property value?
sections.html:
You can appeal informally to Property Assessment or formally to the Board of Equalization and Review, and the county accepted appeals on the current bill's value through December 31, 2026. Start online by entering your address at tax.buncombenc.gov, choosing View Parcel and then Tax Appeal Request, or ask for a mailed form at 828-250-4940.

More than 16,000 appeals were filed on the 2026 reappraisal values. The county says unresolved ones are held and applied to the 2027 reappraisal, and owners do not need to refile unless they received a decision and disagree with it.

  • The board hears owners under G.S. 105-322 and can lower, raise or confirm a value.
  • Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before the board adjourns, or within 15 days after a decision notice was mailed fewer than 15 days before adjournment.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days of adjournment.
  • Next step is the state Property Tax Commission, by written notice within 30 days of the mailed decision.

sections.h2: What property tax relief can Buncombe County owners get?
sections.html:
Buncombe County administers three state relief programs: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferral. Applications are open January 1 through June 1, and each owner can use only one of the three.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the home's appraised value is excluded, for owners who are 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled and within the income limit. The limit for 2026 is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is capped at 4% of income for owners at or under the limit and 5% for incomes up to 150% of it, which the state form prints as $58,200 for 2026. Deferred tax becomes a lien and is due if the owner sells or stops living there.

The county also warns that videos circulating online describe a federal senior property tax exemption. It says no such program exists and urges older owners to apply through the county's official forms. The county's new General Assistance Program, described at buncombenc.gov/gap, helps owners and renters with housing and utility costs while funds last.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Buncombe County house with property tax owed?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the parcel, so it is paid from sale proceeds at or before closing. The lien attaches on the date the property is listed each year, along with penalties, interest and costs. A county can enforce it by a foreclosure action in the county where the land lies.

Ask Tax Collections at 828-250-4910 for the amount due on the parcel before you set a closing date. The county's collections page also references tax lien advertising under G.S. 105-369, so an account left delinquent can end up published. If you have a deferred circuit breaker balance, that deferral comes due on a transfer.

Also check whether your Helene-era value adjustment, any pending appeal or a present-use program affects the bill. A buyer's attorney will want to see the account paid and the deed recorded with the register of deeds at 205 College Street.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Buncombe County?
sections.html:
Buncombe County's estimated population on July 1, 2025 was 277,417, with 142,799 housing units across 656.50 square miles of land. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $391,800 and the owner-occupied rate is 66.2%.

Median household income is $74,436, median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,785, and median gross rent is $1,362. About 12.4% of residents live in poverty and 23.2% are 65 or older, which is the group most likely to qualify for state relief. With a median value near $392,000, the exclusion amounts in state law matter for qualifying owners and can be large compared with the mortgage-free monthly cost of $505.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Buncombe County.

faqs.q: What is the Buncombe County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county rate is 61.54 cents per $100 of assessed value on the 2021 schedule of values. The Unified Fire District adds 17.38 cents and the Asheville City Schools district 11.75 cents where they apply.

faqs.q: When are Buncombe County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are typically due September 1. The county allows payment through January 5 of the next year without penalty, and interest starts on January 6.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Buncombe County value?
faqs.a: The county said appeals on the current bill's value could be filed through December 31, 2026, online at tax.buncombenc.gov or by calling 828-250-4940. Appeals already filed on the 2026 reappraisal stay on hold for 2027.

faqs.q: Why did my Buncombe County value not change in 2026?
faqs.a: A state law delayed the 2026 reappraisal until 2027, so bills use the 2021 values. Unless you added or changed improvements, the value is the same as the prior year.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for Buncombe County tax relief?
faqs.a: Owners who are 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled within the income limit, and permanently and totally disabled veterans. Apply from January 1 to June 1 through the county's exemptions office at 828-250-4915.
